title: Products of surjective affine morphisms are surjective
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $J$ be a small set, and let $g_j:T_j\to S$ be surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] morphisms for $j\in J$. For the product $T=\prod_{j\in J}T_j$ supplied by [lem-trf-affine-infinite-product-existence], the projection $T\to S$ is surjective.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$. By surjectivity [def-weil-surjective-morphism], for each $j\in J$ there exists $t_j\in T_j$ with $g_j(t_j)=s$; choose one such point for each $j$. The induced residue-field homomorphism $a_j:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t_j)$ makes $\kappa(t_j)$ an extension of $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension]. This choice is over the small set $J$; if $J$ is empty there is simply no point to choose.

Apply [lem-trf-family-common-extension-field] to $k=\kappa(s)$ and $L_j=\kappa(t_j)$ with the embeddings $a_j$ from Step 1. Obtain a field $K$, an embedding $b:\kappa(s)\to K$, and embeddings $e_j:\kappa(t_j)\to K$ with $e_j\circ a_j=b$ for all $j$. The family need not be finite, and the residue-field extensions need not be algebraic.

For any scheme point $x$, write $j_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ for its canonical point morphism. Set $q_j=j_{t_j}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(e_j):\operatorname{Spec}K\to T_j$ and $h=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(b):\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$. These are morphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], $g_j\circ j_{t_j}=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(a_j)$. Functoriality of the contravariant spectrum and $e_j\circ a_j=b$ now give explicitly $g_j\circ q_j=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(a_j)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(e_j)=j_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(e_j\circ a_j)=h$. Thus all the $q_j$ are morphisms over the same $S$-structure $h$.

All the $g_j$ are affine, so [lem-trf-affine-infinite-product-existence] supplies their product in schemes over $S$. Apply its defining universal property to the $S$-scheme $(\operatorname{Spec}K,h)$ and the compatible family $(q_j)_j$. It gives $q:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ with $p\circ q=h$, where $p:T\to S$ is the structure morphism. For $J=\varnothing$ this is the same universal property of the terminal object in schemes over $S$; it still gives $p\circ q=h$.

Let $\xi$ be the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The canonical morphism $j_s$ sends its unique source point to $s$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. Since $\operatorname{Spec}(b)$ maps the unique point to the unique point, $h(\xi)=s$. For $t=q(\xi)$ the equality from Step 4 therefore gives $p(t)=(p\circ q)(\xi)=h(\xi)=s$. As $s$ was arbitrary, $p$ is surjective by [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. If $S$ has no points, the same conclusion is vacuous.
